tldr_label: TL;DR — Hormuz attacks mount, oil nears $110 and Egypt offers to defend Saudi Arabia

tldr_bullets.label: Hormuz
tldr_bullets.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels hit a mine and caught fire in the strait on Saturday; the claim has not been independently confirmed. [[TAG:danger:unverified blast]]

tldr_bullets.label: Egypt and the Gulf
tldr_bullets.body: President Sisi asked parliament to authorize military action to defend Saudi Arabia if Riyadh requests it, as Houthi attacks on the kingdom continue.

tldr_bullets.label: Oil
tldr_bullets.body: Brent settled near $109.86 on Friday, its highest close since May according to The Nation, on Middle East supply fears and reduced Russian refining.

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The Nasdaq ended its worst week since June, down 4.5%, as AI and chip stocks slid; the Dow eked out a weekly gain.

tldr_bullets.label: White House
tldr_bullets.body: Press secretary Katie Zacharia is 'transitioning out' after five days; Trump says there is no rush to name a replacement.

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: A CNN source says Kyiv has run out of Patriot interceptors, and drone strikes on ships off Romania are raising fears of spillover into NATO waters. [[TAG:warning:air-defense gap]]

sections.title: Iran War and the Strait of Hormuz
sections.summary: IRGC claims a supertanker hit a mine; CENTCOM insists the strait is open as attacks hit a record

paragraphs.heading: Supertanker blast claim
paragraphs.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy said a tanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude struck a mine on Saturday while using what it called an unauthorized route through the Strait of Hormuz, causing a large explosion and fire, Euronews, Al Arabiya and The New Arab reported. The statement did not name the ship, its flag or any casualties, and alleged the vessel had switched off its tracking systems and had US military support. There was no independent confirmation. [[TAG:danger:unconfirmed]]

paragraphs.heading: Competing traffic counts
paragraphs.body: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said Friday that nearly 400 commercial vessels crossed the strait in the previous seven days and that it 'remains open for business', according to Times Kuwait and The Jerusalem Post. Ship-tracking data tells a different story: Kpler counted 131 crossings in the week to October 14, down from 176 the week before, CNBC reported. An Iranian lawmaker called claims that the strait had reopened 'completely false'. [[TAG:warning:disputed data]]

paragraphs.heading: Record attacks on shipping
paragraphs.body: NBC News reported that attacks on shipping in and around Hormuz have hit a record high, and a British maritime monitor said October is the busiest month for reported attacks since March. UKMTO separately reported two tankers attacked off Saudi Arabia on Friday, one by a rocket-propelled grenade fired from a small boat; all crew were reported safe.

paragraphs.heading: Strike planning and threats
paragraphs.body: US officials told CNN the Pentagon could use the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb if strikes resume; Trump has said he will not resume strikes before the November 3 midterms and has ruled out nuclear weapons and ground troops. Iran's acting oil minister promised 'precise, appropriate retaliatory measures' for any attack on energy sites, and its security council chief threatened UAE data centers and undersea cables, The New Arab and Fox News reported.

sections.sources: Euronews, Al Arabiya, The New Arab, Mehr News, Times Kuwait, The Jerusalem Post, CNBC, NBC News, Iran International, CNN, Fox News, Al Jazeera

sections.title: Saudi Arabia, Yemen and Egypt
sections.summary: Sisi seeks authority to defend Saudi Arabia; Houthis fire missiles at Aden airport

paragraphs.heading: Egypt steps forward
paragraphs.body: Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sisi said Egypt would act to protect Saudi Arabia and asked parliament to convene an emergency session to authorize it, but only if Riyadh requests help, Anadolu and Iran International reported. Sisi said Egypt does not want to attack anyone and would only defend the kingdom. [[TAG:warning:regional widening]]

paragraphs.heading: Houthi campaign
paragraphs.body: Saudi Arabia says Houthi attacks on Riyadh's airport, Aramco headquarters and other sites have killed at least 12 people in the deadliest strike and at least 19 overall, according to AP and PBS. On Friday the Houthis fired two missiles that landed near the runway at Aden International Airport, Yemen's government told Al Jazeera, days after a strike on the Aden presidential compound killed at least five. [[TAG:danger:airports targeted]]

paragraphs.heading: Saudi response and warnings
paragraphs.body: The Saudi-led coalition has struck Houthi-held areas and said it was preparing evacuation warnings for part of Sanaa, CBS News reported. The Houthis have threatened a 'painful' response if the US joins the offensive. UN envoy Hans Grundberg called attacks on civilian airports 'a grave escalation'. Yemeni government forces claim major gains in Marib, which could not be independently verified.

sections.sources: Anadolu, Iran International, AP, PBS, Al Jazeera, CBS News, WRAL

sections.title: Markets: Weekly Wrap
sections.summary: Nasdaq -4.5% on the week as AI fears bite; energy the lone bright spot

paragraphs.heading: Friday's close
paragraphs.body: The S&P 500 fell 1.1% to 7,659.44, the Dow slipped 0.3% to 52,002.41 and the Nasdaq dropped 2.1% to 26,140.03, the Associated Press reported. For the week the S&P lost 1.9% and the Nasdaq 4.5%, snapping a four-week winning streak, while the Dow rose 0.7%. [[TAG:danger:Nasdaq -4.5% week]]

paragraphs.heading: Tech leads the slide
paragraphs.body: The S&P technology sector fell more than 3% Friday, with Micron down 5.6% and Intel down 5.8%, Yahoo Finance reported. TheStreet said worries about an AI bubble are mounting as small caps in the Russell 2000 also sank.

paragraphs.heading: Energy rallies
paragraphs.body: Energy was the best-performing sector, up 2.52% on Friday as crude prices jumped, according to Yahoo Finance. [[TAG:success:energy +2.5%]]

sections.sources: AP, ABC News, Washington Post, Yahoo Finance, TheStreet, Trading Economics

sections.title: Oil, Inflation and the Fed
sections.summary: Brent near $110, highest close since May; Fed seen holding in October but hawkish

paragraphs.heading: Crude surges
paragraphs.body: Brent settled around $109.86 a barrel on Friday and US crude near $101.41, The Rio Times reported, after trading near $105 to $106 earlier in the day. The Nation called it the highest settlement since May 19 and attributed the move to the Middle East conflict and reduced Russian refining capacity after Ukrainian drone strikes. [[TAG:danger:Brent ~$110]]

paragraphs.heading: The Fed's path
paragraphs.body: Minutes from the September meeting showed most officials expect another rate increase by year end. Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin has said one hike may not be enough, while New York Fed President John Williams has signaled no need for urgency, according to CNBC and Chase. Forecasters broadly expect a hold at the October 27–28 meeting. [[TAG:info:hold expected]]

paragraphs.heading: Inflation backdrop
paragraphs.body: September consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier, driven by a 9.1% monthly jump in gasoline, and Yahoo Finance reported that Fed officials say they are troubled by the hot data.

sections.sources: The Rio Times, The Nation, Fortune, OilPriceAPI, CNBC, Chase, Yahoo Finance

sections.title: US Politics
sections.summary: Press secretary out after five days; GOP's $740M blitz fails to shift the midterm map

paragraphs.heading: Press secretary exit
paragraphs.body: A White House official said Katie Zacharia is 'transitioning out' as press secretary after five days, NPR and Al Jazeera reported. Trump said he told her to reconsider the job but denied firing her, and said there is no rush to name a successor. Newsweek reported that Laura Loomer has floated herself for the role. [[TAG:warning:no successor yet]]

paragraphs.heading: Turbulent week
paragraphs.body: Politico reported Trump was consulting allies about replacing chief of staff Susie Wiles after the midterms, which Trump denied, according to US News. Trump also directed the White House counsel to review Alina Habba's claim that Ric Grenell failed to deposit a roughly $6 million donation to the Kennedy Center. Trump separately called off Pete Hegseth's plan to livestream the December 3 execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan.

paragraphs.heading: Midterm outlook
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Republican groups have spent more than $740 million on House and Senate races since Labor Day with little effect, as Democrats lead polling averages in nine of the most competitive Senate races. Kalshi traders gave Democrats about 63% odds of winning the Senate as of October 16. Texas remains close: one poll has Ken Paxton narrowly ahead of James Talarico, while Marist has Talarico up 47 to 45. [[TAG:info:Nov 3 election]]

sections.sources: NPR, Al Jazeera, Newsweek, US News, Washington Post, CNBC, Kalshi, RealClearPolling, Democracy Now

sections.title: Ukraine and Europe
sections.summary: Kyiv out of Patriot interceptors, CNN source says; EU summit ends without budget deal

paragraphs.heading: Air-defense gap
paragraphs.body: A source told CNN that Ukraine has run out of Patriot interceptors and that nearly all ballistic missiles in Russia's latest major attack got through; strikes on Kyiv power plants killed four and injured 25. The exact stockpile has not been made public. [[TAG:danger:no Patriot missiles]]

paragraphs.heading: Spillover fears
paragraphs.body: A drone struck the chemical tanker Wine Trader off Sulina in Romanian waters on October 15, leaving seven crew missing, AP reported. Drones have hit at least seven cargo ships off Romania and Bulgaria in recent weeks, leaving 25 dead or missing; Bulgaria's prime minister said Russia was likely responsible. Poland scrambled fighter jets during overnight Russian strikes on western Ukraine, Al Jazeera reported. [[TAG:warning:NATO waters]]

paragraphs.heading: EU summit
paragraphs.body: EU leaders ended their Brussels summit without a final deal on the 2028–2034 budget, aiming for agreement by year end, according to the Council and Euronews. They backed Zelenskyy and pledged to keep sanctions while Russia's invasion continues, but a €70 billion Ukraine funding gap for next year remains. Bulgaria's prime minister broke ranks to support the Trump-Putin diesel deal others condemned, and leaders clashed over migration.

paragraphs.heading: Strikes on Russia
paragraphs.body: Russia's Defense Ministry said it intercepted 644 Ukrainian drones overnight across several regions, causing flight delays at Moscow airports, as Zelenskyy said Ukraine would keep striking refineries despite Trump's objections.

sections.sources: CNN, Defence Matters, AP, PBS, Washington Times, DTN, Al Jazeera, Euronews, European Council, RFE/RL

sections.title: Asia-Pacific
sections.summary: China expands export controls; carrier drills and missiles near Taiwan keep tensions high

paragraphs.heading: Export controls
paragraphs.body: China plans to add AI, biopharma and solar technologies to its export control list, Nikkei Asia reported. The EU summit separately agreed to develop new trade defense tools aimed at China, Euronews reported. [[TAG:warning:tech controls]]

paragraphs.heading: Military signals
paragraphs.body: China sent its Liaoning carrier group into the western Pacific for training, and Japan tracked the flotilla, The Japan Times reported. The US plans to deploy an anti-ship missile system on Yonaguni, a Japanese island near Taiwan, during joint drills.

paragraphs.heading: Diplomatic chill
paragraphs.body: Beijing and Tokyo remain at odds, including over China's omission of an honorific for Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, the South China Morning Post reported, despite Trump urging Xi Jinping to end the freeze ahead of APEC in November.

sections.sources: Nikkei Asia, The Japan Times, South China Morning Post, Euronews

sections.title: Global Roundup
sections.summary: Ebola passes 9,200 cases in DR Congo; Lebanon fears renewed war; Iran rial slides

paragraphs.heading: Ebola
paragraphs.body: DR Congo has recorded 9,277 confirmed cases and 4,478 deaths in the Bundibugyo-strain outbreak as of October 15, according to ECDC, with no approved vaccine or treatment for this strain. Kenya reported a third case, a relative of its first patient, with no sign of community transmission, Al Jazeera reported. [[TAG:danger:9,277 cases]]

paragraphs.heading: Lebanon
paragraphs.body: Statements from Israeli officials and Hezbollah raised fears of a new war, Arab News reported. Lebanese authorities seized hundreds of kilograms of explosives, which Hezbollah acknowledged were its own, according to Middle East Monitor. President Joseph Aoun said US-mediated talks with Israel have slowed but not stopped.

paragraphs.heading: Iran's economy
paragraphs.body: The rial trades around 2.65 million to the dollar on the open market, against an official rate near 1.82 million, Iran International reported, and an Iranian trade official warned import curbs could deepen shortages. Iranian exports to Pakistan face a temporary halt over banking sanctions.

paragraphs.heading: Americas
paragraphs.body: Colombia resumed electricity sales to Ecuador after more than a month, The Rio Times reported. [[TAG:success:power restored]]

sections.sources: ECDC, WHO, Al Jazeera, UN News, Arab News, Middle East Monitor, Times of Israel, Iran International, Trend, The Rio Times
